metadata.title: Accelerating Stochastic Gradient Descent using Predictive Variance Reduction
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Finite-Sum Optimization
nodes.statement: $\min_w P(w)$ where $P(w) := \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \psi_i(w)$, with $\psi_i:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the average of n vector-valued loss functions over a parameter w.

nodes.name: Least Squares and Regularized Logistic Regression
nodes.statement: Squared loss $\psi_i(w) = (w^\top x_i - y_i)^2$ yields least squares; $\psi_i(w) = \ln(1 + \exp(-w^\top x_i y_i)) + 0.5\lambda w^\top w$ yields regularized logistic regression.
nodes.statement_clean: Two standard machine-learning instances of the finite-sum problem.

nodes.name: Smoothness of $\psi_i$
nodes.statement: $\psi_i$ is $L$-smooth: $\psi_i(w) - \psi_i(w') - 0.5L\|w - w'\|^2 \leq \nabla \psi_i(w')^\top (w - w')$.
nodes.statement_clean: Each component function has Lipschitz-continuous gradient with constant L.

nodes.name: Strong Convexity of $P$
nodes.statement: $P$ is $\gamma$-strongly convex: $P(w) - P(w') - 0.5\gamma\|w - w'\|_2^2 \geq \nabla P(w')^\top (w - w')$, where $L \geq \gamma \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: P satisfies a quadratic lower bound around any point with parameter gamma.

nodes.name: Gradient Descent (GD)
nodes.statement: Full-batch update $w^{(t)} = w^{(t-1)} - \eta_t \nabla P(w^{(t-1)}) = w^{(t-1)} - \frac{\eta_t}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\nabla \psi_i(w^{(t-1)})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Iterate by stepping along the negative full gradient of P.

nodes.name: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
nodes.statement: At each iteration $t$, draw $i_t$ uniformly at random from $\{1,\dots,n\}$ and update $w^{(t)} = w^{(t-1)} - \eta_t \nabla \psi_{i_t}(w^{(t-1)})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Replace the full gradient with a single sampled component gradient at each step.

nodes.name: Generalized Stochastic Gradient Update
nodes.statement_clean: General SGD framework with any unbiased stochastic gradient estimator.

nodes.name: Convergence Trade-off Between SGD and GD
nodes.statement: With constant $\eta < 1/L$, GD has linear convergence $O((1-\gamma/L)^t)$. SGD typically requires $\eta_t = O(1/t)$, giving slower sub-linear rate $O(1/t)$ due to inherent variance.
nodes.statement_clean: GD is fast per-iteration but expensive; SGD is cheap per-iteration but converges slowly.

nodes.name: Stochastic Average Gradient (SAG)
nodes.statement: Variance-reduction SGD that maintains a stored gradient per training example, achieving linear convergence for smooth strongly convex losses.
nodes.statement_clean: Earlier variance-reduced stochastic method storing all per-sample gradients.

nodes.name: Stochastic Dual Coordinate Ascent (SDCA)
nodes.statement: Dual coordinate ascent on the SDCA dual variables $\alpha_i$; achieves linear convergence for smooth strongly convex regularized losses; requires storing dual variables.
nodes.statement_clean: Dual stochastic method achieving linear convergence; requires per-sample dual storage.

nodes.name: Average Gradient Snapshot
nodes.statement: $\tilde\mu = \nabla P(\tilde w) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \nabla \psi_i(\tilde w)$ computed once per outer stage at snapshot $\tilde w$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mean gradient evaluated at the snapshot reference point.

nodes.name: SVRG Update Rule
nodes.statement: $w^{(t)} = w^{(t-1)} - \eta_t (\nabla \psi_{i_t}(w^{(t-1)}) - \nabla \psi_{i_t}(\tilde w) + \tilde\mu)$, drawing $i_t$ uniformly.
nodes.statement_clean: Variance-reduced stochastic update using snapshot-corrected gradient.

nodes.name: Unbiasedness of SVRG Update
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[w^{(t)}\mid w^{(t-1)}] = w^{(t-1)} - \eta_t \nabla P(w^{(t-1)})$, so the SVRG update is an unbiased estimator of the GD step.
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional expectation of the SVRG step equals the gradient-descent step.

nodes.name: Auxiliary-Function Derivation of SVRG
nodes.statement: Define $\tilde\psi_i(w) = \psi_i(w) - (\nabla \psi_i(\tilde w) - \tilde\mu)^\top w$. Since $\sum_i (\nabla \psi_i(\tilde w) - \tilde\mu) = 0$, $P(w) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \tilde\psi_i(w)$, and standard SGD on $\tilde\psi_i$ recovers the SVRG update.
nodes.statement_clean: SVRG is equivalent to standard SGD applied to a control-variate-shifted problem.

nodes.name: Variance Vanishes at the Optimum
nodes.statement: If $\tilde w, w^{(t)} \to w^*$ then $\tilde\mu \to 0$ and $\nabla \psi_i(w^{(t-1)}) - \nabla \psi_i(\tilde w) + \tilde\mu \to 0$, so the variance of the update decays as the iterates approach the optimum.
nodes.statement_clean: The corrected gradient converges to zero as the snapshot and current iterate approach w*.

nodes.name: Stochastic Variance Reduced Gradient (SVRG)
nodes.statement: Two-loop iterative method with periodic full-gradient snapshots and variance-reduced inner SGD updates using the snapshot.
nodes.statement_clean: SVRG: outer loop maintains snapshot $\tilde w$ and full gradient $\tilde\mu$; inner loop runs $m$ variance-reduced SGD steps.
output: Snapshot iterates $\tilde w_s$ converging geometrically to $w^*$
nodes.pseudocode:
for s = 1, 2, ...: set $	ilde w = 	ilde w_{s-1}$; compute $	ilde\mu =  rac{1}{n}\sum_i 
abla \psi_i(	ilde w)$; set $w_0 = 	ilde w$; for t = 1..m: pick $i_t$ uniformly; $w_t = w_{t-1} - \eta(
abla \psi_{i_t}(w_{t-1}) - 
abla \psi_{i_t}(	ilde w) + 	ilde\mu)$; option I: $	ilde w_s = w_m$; option II: $	ilde w_s = w_t$ for random $t \in \{0,\dots,m-1\}$.

nodes.name: Initialize Snapshot
nodes.statement: Initialize $\tilde w_0$.

nodes.name: Outer Loop: Refresh Snapshot Gradient
nodes.statement: For $s = 1, 2, \dots$: set $\tilde w = \tilde w_{s-1}$, compute $\tilde\mu = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \nabla \psi_i(\tilde w)$, and set $w_0 = \tilde w$.

nodes.name: Inner Loop: Variance-Reduced SGD Updates
nodes.statement: For $t = 1, \dots, m$: pick $i_t \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ uniformly; update $w_t = w_{t-1} - \eta(\nabla \psi_{i_t}(w_{t-1}) - \nabla \psi_{i_t}(\tilde w) + \tilde\mu)$.

nodes.name: Snapshot Selection (Option I or II)
nodes.statement: Option I: set $\tilde w_s = w_m$. Option II: set $\tilde w_s = w_t$ for $t$ chosen uniformly at random in $\{0,\dots,m-1\}$.

nodes.name: SVRG Geometric Convergence
nodes.statement: Under convex smooth $\psi_i$, $\gamma$-strongly convex $P$, and $\alpha = \frac{1}{\gamma\eta(1-2L\eta)m} + \frac{2L\eta}{1-2L\eta} < 1$, $\mathbb{E}\,P(\tilde w_s) \leq \mathbb{E}\,P(w^*) + \alpha^s [P(\tilde w_0) - P(w^*)]$.
nodes.statement_clean: SVRG (option II) has geometric convergence in expectation when m is large enough.

nodes.name: Proof of SVRG Geometric Convergence
nodes.statement: Bound $\mathbb{E}\|v_t\|_2^2$ in terms of $P(w_{t-1}) - P(w^*)$ and $P(\tilde w) - P(w^*)$ using smoothness; expand $\mathbb{E}\|w_t - w^*\|_2^2$, sum over $t$, and apply strong convexity to get the per-stage contraction $\alpha$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smoothness gives a per-step variance bound; summing over the inner loop and applying strong convexity yields the geometric contraction.

nodes.name: Introduce Auxiliary Function $g_i$
nodes.statement: Define $g_i(w) = \psi_i(w) - \psi_i(w^*) - \nabla \psi_i(w^*)^\top (w - w^*)$. Then $g_i(w^*) = \min_w g_i(w)$ since $\nabla g_i(w^*) = 0$.

nodes.name: Smoothness Yields Per-Component Gradient Bound
nodes.statement:
From $0 = g_i(w^*) \leq \min_\eta [g_i(w) - \eta\|
abla g_i(w)\|_2^2 + 0.5L\eta^2 \|
abla g_i(w)\|_2^2]$, conclude $\|
abla \psi_i(w) - 
abla \psi_i(w^*)\|_2^2 \leq 2L[\psi_i(w) - \psi_i(w^*) - 
abla \psi_i(w^*)^	op (w - w^*)]$.

nodes.name: Sum Over $i$ to Obtain Eq. (8)
nodes.statement:
Summing the per-component bound and using $
abla P(w^*) = 0$ gives $n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\|
abla \psi_i(w) - 
abla \psi_i(w^*)\|_2^2 \leq 2L[P(w) - P(w^*)]$.

nodes.name: Bound $\mathbb{E}\|v_t\|_2^2$
nodes.statement: Let $v_t = \nabla \psi_{i_t}(w_{t-1}) - \nabla \psi_{i_t}(\tilde w) + \tilde\mu$. Using $\|a+b\|^2 \leq 2\|a\|^2 + 2\|b\|^2$, $\mathbb{E}\|\xi - \mathbb{E}\xi\|^2 \leq \mathbb{E}\|\xi\|^2$, and (8): $\mathbb{E}\|v_t\|_2^2 \leq 4L[P(w_{t-1}) - P(w^*) + P(\tilde w) - P(w^*)]$.

nodes.name: Expand $\mathbb{E}\|w_t - w^*\|_2^2$
nodes.statement: Conditioned on $w_{t-1}$, $\mathbb{E}\|w_t - w^*\|_2^2 \leq \|w_{t-1} - w^*\|_2^2 - 2\eta(1-2L\eta)[P(w_{t-1}) - P(w^*)] + 4L\eta^2 [P(\tilde w) - P(w^*)]$, using convexity of $P$ and the bound on $\mathbb{E}\|v_t\|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Sum Over Inner Loop and Apply Strong Convexity
nodes.statement: Summing over $t = 1, \dots, m$ and using option II together with $\|\tilde w - w^*\|_2^2 \leq (2/\gamma)[P(\tilde w) - P(w^*)]$ yields $2\eta(1-2L\eta)m\,\mathbb{E}[P(\tilde w_s) - P(w^*)] \leq 2(\gamma^{-1} + 2Lm\eta^2)\,\mathbb{E}[P(\tilde w) - P(w^*)]$.

nodes.name: Recursion Yields Geometric Decay
nodes.statement: Dividing gives $\mathbb{E}[P(\tilde w_s) - P(w^*)] \leq \alpha\,\mathbb{E}[P(\tilde w_{s-1}) - P(w^*)]$, hence $\leq \alpha^s\,\mathbb{E}[P(\tilde w_0) - P(w^*)]$.

nodes.name: Complexity Comparison: $L/\gamma = n$
nodes.statement: With condition number $L/\gamma = n$, taking $\eta = 0.1/L$ and $m = O(n)$ gives $\alpha = 1/2$, so SVRG processes $n \ln(1/\epsilon)$ examples to reach accuracy $\epsilon$, matching SAG and SDCA, vs. $n^2 \ln(1/\epsilon)$ for batch GD.
nodes.statement_clean: SVRG matches SAG/SDCA complexity and improves on batch GD by a factor of n.

nodes.name: Extension to Smooth Non-Strongly Convex and Nonconvex Cases
nodes.statement: For smooth non-strongly-convex problems, SVRG attains $O(1/T)$, improving over SGD's $O(1/\sqrt{T})$. For nonconvex problems (e.g. neural nets), starting near a local minimum and using SVRG accelerates local convergence; if the problem is locally strongly convex, Theorem 1 applies.

nodes.name: Regularized Finite-Sum (SDCA Formulation)
nodes.statement: $w^* = \arg\min_w P(w)$, $P(w) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \phi_i(w) + 0.5\lambda w^\top w$, with each $\phi_i$ convex.
nodes.statement_clean: L2-regularized finite-sum convex objective addressed by SDCA.

nodes.name: Dual Representation at Optimum
nodes.statement: $w^* = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \alpha_i^*$ where the dual variables satisfy $\alpha_i^* = -\frac{1}{\lambda n}\nabla \phi_i(w^*)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Optimum decomposes into per-sample dual contributions proportional to per-sample gradients.

nodes.name: SDCA Dual Update Rule
nodes.statement: Update $\alpha_\ell^{(t)} = \alpha_i^{(t-1)} - \eta_t(\nabla \phi_i(w^{(t-1)}) + \lambda n \alpha_i^{(t-1)})$ for $\ell = i$ and $\alpha_\ell^{(t)} = \alpha_\ell^{(t-1)}$ for $\ell \neq i$, then $w^{(t)} = w^{(t-1)} + (\alpha_i^{(t)} - \alpha_i^{(t-1)})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Coordinate-ascent style update of dual variables that allows non-vanishing learning rates.

nodes.name: SDCA as a Variance Reduction Method
nodes.statement:
Both the SGD-style update (12) and the SDCA update (13) are unbiased for $
abla P(w^{(t-1)})$. As $(w,\alpha) 	o (w^*, \alpha^*)$, $
abla \phi_i(w) + \lambda n \alpha_i 	o 0$, so $ rac{1}{n}\sum_i (
abla \phi_i(w) + \lambda n \alpha_i)^2 	o 0$, paralleling SVRG: SDCA is a variance-reduction method for SGD.
nodes.statement_clean: SDCA's update variance vanishes at the optimum, mirroring the SVRG mechanism.

nodes.name: MNIST Multiclass Logistic Regression (Convex)
nodes.statement: L2-regularized multiclass logistic regression on MNIST with $\lambda = 10^{-4}$, $m = 2n$. SVRG with a single relatively large $\eta$ converges smoothly faster than fixed-rate SGD, matches SDCA on training-loss residual $P(w) - P(w^*)$, and shows decaying update variance unlike SGD.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex MNIST experiment confirming SVRG matches SDCA and beats best-tuned SGD.

nodes.name: Convex Experiments on rcv1, protein, covtype, CIFAR-10
nodes.statement: L2-regularized logistic regression on rcv1.binary, protein, covtype.binary, and CIFAR-10 ($\lambda = 10^{-3}$ for CIFAR, $10^{-5}$ otherwise). SVRG is competitive with SDCA and clearly outperforms best-tuned SGD on training-loss residual and test error.
nodes.statement_clean: Additional convex datasets confirm SVRG's advantage over best-tuned SGD and parity with SDCA.

nodes.name: Nonconvex Neural-Net Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10
nodes.statement: Single-hidden-layer (100 sigmoid units) neural nets trained on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with mini-batches of size 10, $m = 5n$, $\lambda = 10^{-4}$ (MNIST) and $10^{-3}$ (CIFAR). SVRG reduces variance and converges faster than best-tuned SGD with rate scheduling.
nodes.statement_clean: Nonconvex neural-net experiments showing SVRG advantage where SDCA/SAG cannot apply.
